title: Adaptive Pre-warm & SLO Lanes for Dedicated Capacity — PRD (Draft)
content:
Context and problem

Customers run mixed-criticality workloads on Dedicated pools: some requests are latency-sensitive (live chat assistants, search reranking), others are throughput-oriented or batch. Today we offer static reserved capacity + blunt burst lanes. This leads to two recurring problems:

- Cold-container/model-warmup latency for unexpected spikes causing SLO violations.
- Inefficient cost when customers over-provision to avoid the cold-start risk.
- Hard tradeoffs in tenant isolation: strict isolation wastes GPU time, loose isolation can hurt critical tenants during surges.

Goal

Design an adaptive pre-warm and SLO-lane system that:
- Proactively maintains lightweight warm capacity based on tenant SLO profiles and short-term forecasts.
- Provides configurable SLO lanes (e.g., gold/silver/bronze) that map to pre-warm and fallback policies.
- Minimizes cost by sharing warm buffers across compatible tenants while preserving isolation guarantees via soft quotas and graceful preemption.
- Exposes APIs and Console UX for operators and customers to configure profiles, view warm pool utilization, and run canary rollouts.

Success metrics (initial targets)

- Reduce cold-start SLO violations for latency-sensitive workloads by >= 70% in first month after rollout.
- Keep additional warm-hours cost delta for most customers below 12% compared to baseline over steady-state workloads.
- Provide observability: dashboard for warm-pool fill rate, forecast accuracy, and preemptions with <1s telemetry latency.

Design principles

1) Tenant SLO profiles drive behavior: customers declare per-route SLO tiers (p99 latency target, max allowed cold-start rate, priority).
2) Lightweight warm units: pre-warm should aim to keep model processes and caches primed rather than full dedicated GPUs where possible (e.g., colocated micro-pools or fast-start containers).
3) Predict-and-prewarm: short-horizon forecasting (1m–30m) using request rate, pattern heuristics, and signals from customer telemetry.
4) Shared warm buffer with soft isolation: warm capacity is pooled across tenants with rules to ensure gold lane has access guarantees; soft preemption used during constraints.
5) Safe fallback: when warm pools are exhausted, fall back to compatible model variants or queue-with-shed strategies rather than immediate hard failures.

System components (high level)

- SLO Profile API: declarative per-route JSON config (see example below).
- Forecast engine: lightweight time-series predictor + sudden-spike detector.
- Pre-warm controller: translates forecasts into allocation actions (start containers, inflate KV cache, pin attention layers) and manages warm buffer.
- Warm buffer manager: pooling layer that tracks units, ownership shares, and soft-eviction policies.
- Routing/Serving hooks: runtime checks warm status and applies fast-path for warm requests; records telemetry for model warmness and cold-starts.
- Console + Metrics: per-tenant warm pool dashboard, SLO compliance, forecast vs actual.

SLO Profile API (proposal)

- Example payload:
  {
    "route": "/chat/prompt",
    "slo_tier": "gold",            // gold | silver | bronze
    "p99_latency_ms": "150",
    "cold_start_tolerance_percent": "1",
    "burst_priority": "high",     // used by warm buffer arbiter
    "prewarm_window_minutes": "5" // lookahead window to ensure warm units
  }

Behavior by tier (defaults)

- Gold: aggressive prewarm (forecasted + margin), guaranteed soft-allocated warm units, number of allowed preemptions <= 1/hour, fallback to pinned smaller variant only as last resort.
- Silver: opportunistic prewarm (forecasted only), allowed to use shared warm pool with medium preempt priority, fallback to compatible variant.
- Bronze: no guaranteed prewarm, can use leftover warm units when idle, default to batch/queued processing for spikes.

Allocation & isolation strategy

- Warm Unit: smallest practicable warmed state (e.g., lightweight process with model weights loaded to CPU or quantized variant already resident); track as 1 warm unit.
- Soft Quotas: allocate minimum warm units per tenant based on SLO and commit tier. Soft quotas are enforced as priority ordering rather than absolute locks.
- Preemption: when pool constrained, preemption prefers oldest non-gold warm units; record preemption events in audit log. Preemption handlers must gracefully checkpoint KV caches where possible.
- Burst lanes: short-lived dedicated warm lanes can be provisioned for predictable events (cron or known campaigns) using API or Console. Those lanes are scheduled ahead and billed separately.

Pre-warm actions (examples)

- Start minimal container with weights memory-mapped and KV cache warmed with recent prefixes.
- Warm tokenizers and decode tables in user process.
- Prepare quantized kernels if variant switching planned.

Runtime behavior sequence

1) Forecast predicts X warm units for tenant T in next W minutes.
2) Pre-warm controller attempts to ensure inventory: either create lightweight warm units or reserve pool slots.
3) Serving runtime checks request: if warm unit available -> route to fast-path (low-latency).
4) If not and fallbacks allowed -> route to compatible quantized variant or queue with priority.
5) Telemetry increments cold-start counters; autoscaler learns and adjusts.

Console UX changes

- New "Warm Pools" view per-dedicated cluster: pooled capacity, warm unit distribution, forecast graph, preemption log.
- Per-tenant SLO profile editor + historical SLO compliance heatmap.
- Single-click: create an ad-hoc burst lane for a tenant for N minutes.

API changes (surface-level)

- POST /v1/dedicated/slo-profiles -> create/update SLO profile.
- GET /v1/dedicated/warm-pools -> inventory and utilization.
- POST /v1/dedicated/burst-lanes -> temporary dedicated pre-warm lane with duration and budget.

Metrics and observability

Instrumented metrics (must emit to Prom):
- warm_units_total (labels: pool, tenant, tier)
- warm_unit_fill_percent (pool)
- forecast_accuracy_{1m,5m,30m}
- cold_start_rate (labels: tenant, route, tier)
- preemptions_total (labels: tenant, reason)
- additional_cost_estimate_hours (per-tenant)

Rollout plan (phased)

1) Canary (internal tenants): enable for internal test clusters only, collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
2) Beta partners: open to selected customers, require optional opt-in API flag, run 4-week pilot.
3) General availability: default policy enabled but conservative margins; expose UI for opt-out.

Acceptance criteria

- Canary shows >= 50% reduction in cold-start SLO violations for targeted routes.
- Forecast engine F1 score above baseline model for 1m/5m horizons.
- Warm pool metrics visible and actionable in Console.
- No observed > 10% increase in GPU-hours billed across pilot tenants unless they opted into burst lanes.

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: Forecasts mispredict and create cost spikes. Mitigation: conservative safety margins, cost caps per-tenant, and auto-shutdown policies.
- Risk: Shared warm pool leads to noisy-neighbor warm churn. Mitigation: strict preemption policies, tenant-affinity heuristics, and experimental pinning toggles.
- Risk: Complexity leads to hard-to-debug SLO regressions. Mitigation: comprehensive telemetry, canary runbooks, and revert flags.

Open questions / TODOs

- How to quantify warm-unit equivalence across model families? (e.g., Llama-2-13B vs 70B) TODO: define normalized warm unit metric.
- Billing model for warm units and burst lanes — per-hour vs per-use? Finance input required (ask @Priya).
- Interactions with Dedicated reserved capacity billing and contractual SLAs — legal review required.

Stakeholders

- Product: Aisha Patel (owner), Marco Li
- Serving runtime: Ethan Romero
- Infra & Autoscaler: Lena Fischer
- Developer Experience / Console: Priya Desai
- Sales / Customer Success: Julian Meyer (pilot coordination)

Timeline (high level)

- Design spec: 3 weeks (Feb 14–Mar 7)
- Implementation (core): 8–10 weeks (Mar 10–May 16)
- Pilot & tuning: 4–6 weeks (May 19–Jun 30)

Appendix — simple forecast heuristics to start

- Short-horizon exponential smoothing of request counts with spike detector (threshold of X sigma).
- Fast fallback: if spike detector fires and no pre-warm available, trigger emergency ephemeral warm (best-effort) and mark cost.

Notes / scratch

- Link to experiments: CONFLUENCE:dedicated-prewarm-experiments
- Slack thread: #dedicated-prewarm (see Feb 5 discussion)
- Next immediate action: align billing and legal, and run microbench to measure warm-unit warmup time per model type.

(End of draft)
